en: Hi friends! Today we have the munchmill, and I'll try to explain it
in as much detail as possible.

over which.

many b-boys wondered too, and there's no single answer.

the right leg over the left.

So what's the answer?
It doesn't matter which leg goes over which.

power move combos.

Let's continue.

always have to remember.

you need to tuck the legs earlier, before you're on your back. So
we tuck the legs at this moment.
The next detail: you
absolutely must land on the left shoulder. Look:
now I'll do the first version and land straight on my back.
And it turns out I immediately
fly over onto the right shoulder, and I think that's wrong.
I think it's very important to focus on landing on the left
shoulder on the entry, so you get a kind of rocking boat from the left shoulder to the right,
and then the munchmill. Watch closely:
this is the side I land on. I won't drop it now on purpose,
I'll do it so you can see the moment.
I'll show it again.
Exactly like this. And pay
attention: always put down the left shoulder and roll off it.
So, guys, if you understand the main concept I'm about to
explain, munchmill will be a very simple move for you.
If you work with your legs first and then your body, you'll
probably bruise your ribs, like I and many other guys did
back in the day, and you'll start to fear this move. Don't go for the leg push
until you can properly do munchmill, until you can do
1, 2, 3 rotations. First you need to understand this.
Look: in Russian-speaking breaking
munchmill is called 'the barrel'.
Think about it: why a barrel?
Ever seen a barrel roll?
A barrel doesn't jerk, doesn't jump, it just rolls.
So your first rotations, your first steps in munchmill should be exactly
a roll. No leg work like this at all.
You're tucked, knees close to the shoulders, in this position.
And you should do the first rotations like tumbling, tumbling. No
speedy munchmill — just rolling over, just rolling over. I'll try
to show you slowly.
This
is how we do it: barely moving, no rush, carefully making sure
we don't crash into the ribs.

crash into your ribs. Think about it and do it right. Guys, now

especially at first.
Especially at first.
You need to work from the hip.
It's the hip that works.
Roughly speaking, the angle at the knee hardly changes.
Purely the hip works.

as it can possibly, damn, be.

do it. It's the same story as with the windmill over the head, when guys
bruise their legs because they don't finish the turn in time.
Same thing: the push comes from the hip.
Not like this, but roughly from here to here.
From the hip, from the hip. And small.
Understand: the leg push is purely there to
lift yourself onto the head from this position.

get up onto the head.

straight into the fourth. I think that way you'll quickly get how to do multiple rotations. Guys,
I've already talked about safety in munchmill and crashing into the ribs, but if
you keep crashing, I suggest training on tatami, on mats, on firm mats.
Wrestling tatami —
if you have them, great.
If not, go to a gymnastics gym and train there.
Next. Many people bruise their shoulder.

What's the solution?
Either a hoodie that stays dry and a slippery floor.
If you don't have that, stick on a regular plaster.
Not an antibacterial one, but a thick one like this.
You can put a few layers where you scrape your shoulder.
Then a T-shirt and a hoodie over it.
I think you won't have problems with scrapes anymore.
Next. Many people scrape their hands, right?
Put plasters on the hands too.
In short, on every spot you scrape in munchmill, put a plaster
for training. I promise you won't have problems with it anymore.
That's the life hack, as they say.
That's it, guys — go smash it!
